title: Launch Traffic Orchestra — Scratchpad (compact)
body:
Purpose and context:
This is a compact scratchpad for the ‘Traffic Orchestra’ mini-roll scheduled for Dec 15–16, 2026. It blends a short rollout calendar, a tight preflight checklist, signal thresholds for go/no-go decisions, and a first-pass release-notes draft. Intended for the launch conductor and the on-call crew — goal is to be short, actionable, and easy to paste into the run channel.

High-level objective:
- Ramp new routing policy + shard split to reduce tail latency for short chat requests while keeping overall QPS stable.
- Validate automated fallback to smaller model family under high P99 latency.

Conductor and primary contacts:
- Launch conductor: Anika Rao (primary)
- Run lead: Marcus Liu (safety lane)
- SRE point: Sophie Adler (observability & alerts)
- Serving owner: Diego Martínez (model variants / infra)
- Exec watch: Priya Natarajan (on-call for exec escalations)

Compact rollout calendar (UTC):
- T-72h (Dec 12, 09:00): Final smoke artifacts baked and sanity tests green.
- T-48h (Dec 13, 10:30): Canary infra prepared: 2 canary pools (stable/experiment), traffic switch scripts staged.
- T-24h (Dec 14, 11:00): Dry-run: switch 0.5% -> 1% traffic to experiment in staging replica, confirm metrics reporting.
- T-6h (Dec 15, 06:00): Preflight checklist run; all teams on standby.
- T0 (Dec 15, 12:00): Start live mini-roll: 1% -> 5% -> 10% -> 25% (30m hold each)
- T+6h (Dec 15, 18:00): If stable, continue to 50% (1h hold), then gradual 75%/100% next day if no regressions.
- T+24h (Dec 16, 12:00): Post-roll forensic snapshot and lightweight retro.

Preflight checklist (quick-pass):
- Code / infra
  - [ ] Release artifact tag exists: serving-runtime v2026.12.2-exp-traffic
  - [ ] Canary pools provisioned: canary-us-west2-1, canary-eu-west1-1
  - [ ] Roll scripts uploaded: s3://rbx-release-scripts/traffic-orchestra/dec-2026/
- Observability
  - [ ] Baseline dashboard created for canary vs stable (latency, error rate, throughput, qps)
  - [ ] Traces sampled for experiment path (min 500 spans/min)
  - [ ] KV cache hit rate reporting enabled (prefix caching)
- Safety
  - [ ] Fallback variant configured (model-small-q4_0 as secondary)
  - [ ] Rate limiter leash set: global throttle at +10% over baseline
  - [ ] Pager rotation for launch window in place (SRE + serving)
- Communication
  - [ ] Run channel created: #run-traffic-orchestra-dec15 (pinned playbook)
  - [ ] Exec summary draft shared to /exec-watch 30m before T0
- Test & validation
  - [ ] Synthetic load tests (90th/99th percentiles) complete and saved to artifacts
  - [ ] Smoke tests for edge cases (tool-calls, streaming, long-context) green

Go / No‑Go thresholds (per 30m hold window):
- Automatic NO-GO (immediate rollback):
  - error-rate increase > 1.5x baseline AND absolute error-rate > 0.5%
  - P99 latency increase > 2x baseline OR P99 > 2000ms
  - increased customer-facing 5xx alerts in last 10m (>3 new incidents)
- Manual review (pause & triage):
  - sustained P50 increase > 2x but P99 stable (investigate queuing)
  - 5–10% degradation in embeddings throughput linked to kv-cache miss pattern
- Continue (proceed):
  - all critical signals within thresholds for two consecutive hold windows

Sanity verification commands (quick cheatsheet):
- view canary dashboards: curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \"https://observability.internal/dashboards/traffic-orchestra-canary?range=30m\"
- snapshot traces: scripts/collect-traces.sh --from now-30m --to now --output /tmp/traces-canary.json
- switch traffic (dry-run flag): python ops/switch_traffic.py --pool experiment --percent 5 --dry-run
- force rollback (immediate): python ops/switch_traffic.py --pool stable --percent 100 --reason \"auto-rollback\"

Rollback procedure (fast path):
1) Announce rollback in #run-traffic-orchestra-dec15 with reason and immediate ETA.
2) Execute: python ops/switch_traffic.py --pool stable --percent 100 --reason \"rollback\". Monitor for 2min.
3) If traffic switch fails, manually set LB weighting via infra console (ops/infra-handbook#lb-weighting).
4) Open incident in PagerDuty with tag release:traffic-orchestra + link to rollback timeline.
5) Post-mortem: short doc in Confluence within 24h, include smoketest artifacts and traces.

Release notes (first-pass — to be polished by product comms):
- Title: Traffic Orchestra: smarter short-request routing + tail latency reductions (Dec 2026)
- Summary: Introduce tiered routing policy that favors low-latency model family for short chat contexts, plus shard split to reduce hot-key effects. Expected impact: lower P95/P99 for short interactions and marginal cost savings via fewer long-context activations.
- User visible changes: No API changes. Customers may see improved latency on short chat flows.
- Rollout plan: progressive canary on Dec 15–16 with automatic fallback and throttles.
- Known limitations: First 24h may show transient KV-cache warmup leading to slightly elevated P50. Long context sessions may see unchanged latency.
- Callouts: If you see regressions, contact #support-llm and mention release id RBX-2026-traffic-orchestra.

Open questions / risks to track (brief):
- cache-warmpattern: Do we want a manual warmup run for high-traffic prefixes pre-T0? (Marcus to propose script)
- autoscaler interplay: Will autoscaler scale down canary pools aggressively during 30m holds and skew metrics? (SRE to confirm min-pool-size)
- downstream partners: A small fraction of partner integrations run through a proxy that strips keepalive headers — could that interact with new route affinity. (Diego to follow up)

Post-roll items (T+24h):
- Collect 48h telemetry snapshot and run regression evals against critical prompt set.
- Update Optimize with final batching/quant suggestion if unit cost shifts.
- Retro: 30m lightweight + 2h deep-dive if any incidents.

Quick NOTES TO SELF (messy):
- If we see P99 blip right after switching -> check KV cache warming and hot-shard metric (serving.kv.hot_shard_hits)
- Keep fallback model ready at latest quantized build; the smaller variant tends to have different tokenization quirks (watch for token drift in evals)

End (pasteable checklist for channel):
- T-6h: run preflight checklist (Anika)
- T-0: start 1% -> 5% -> 10% -> 25% (Marcus run switches)
- On anomaly: Sophie triages, Diego prepares rollback if needed
- Post: artifacts -> Confluence -> retro

(Will iterate this doc after the first dry-run; trying to keep it compact for channel consumption.)
